title: What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
web_title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Inside Every Segment — Products, Customers & Real-World Examples
question: What does each part of PCBL actually make, for whom, at what price and with what share of the group’s revenue and profit, and which parts carry the economics today?

epigraph.quote: “While the tyre business is based on pass-through, in the non-tyre business in India, we have been successful in increasing prices over the last few months.”
epigraph.author: Nilesh Koul, Managing Director, PCBL Chemical Q4 FY26 earnings call, 30 April 2026

web_blocks.html: PCBL reports four operating segments under Ind AS 108. They are Carbon Black (five plants), Power (captive co-generation, with surplus sold), Chemicals (Aquapharm) and Battery Chemical (Nanovace, a separate segment since FY2025) [3]. To customers the group presents three platforms: Rubber & Specialty Blacks, Specialty & Solutions (Aquapharm), and Battery Chemicals & Conductive Materials [3]. We take them in turn: how much revenue and profit each carries, what volumes each moves, where each sells and which plants make it. Each segment then gets one end-to-end worked example. The chapter ends with our judgment on which segments carry the economics and which are options.

web_blocks.title: How much revenue and profit each segment carries

web_blocks.caption: Segment revenue, profit and assets, audited consolidated; ₹ crore
headers: FY2026 segment profit before interest and tax (share)
FY2026 pre-tax return on segment assets
web_blocks.takeaway: Shares are computed from the audited segment note [3][2]. Segment profit is before ₹275.32 crore of unallocated expenses and before finance costs, so the 9.3% total return on segment assets is not the group’s ROCE. Power’s inter-segment sales (₹130.69 crore in FY2026) are priced at the external purchase price and are on top of the external figure [3]. In FY2025 the profit split was 80.6%, 14.4% and 5.1% for carbon black, power and chemicals (segment profit ₹1,042.35 crore, ₹185.94 crore and ₹65.59 crore) [2]. The Q2 FY27 revenue mix was 79%, 4% and 17% [18].

web_blocks.html: The table shows a business with two faces. Carbon black is 79.5% of revenue and 73.8% of segment profit. Its segment margin fell from 15.3% to 11.1% in a year (profit before interest and tax of ₹721 crore against ₹1,042 crore) while its revenue fell only 4.3% [3][2]. Power is 2.9% of revenue and 24.4% of segment profit on 5.6% of segment assets, a 40.8% pre-tax return. Chemicals is 17.6% of revenue and 40.3% of segment assets but 1.8% of segment profit. That is a 0.4% pre-tax return on ₹4,226 crore, or 2.6% if the ₹91.82 crore a year of acquisition-related amortisation is added back (our arithmetic from the audited note) [3]. Battery chemical has no revenue, a ₹0.15 crore loss and ₹246 crore of assets, which is capital waiting for a product.

web_blocks.caption: The only published EBITDA split: Aquapharm versus the rest of the group; ₹ crore, company definition (includes other income)
headers: Rest of group EBITDA (carbon black, power, corporate)
web_blocks.takeaway: Aquapharm’s share of EBITDA is below its share of revenue in every period because its margin (13.7%, 11.2% and 10.8%) trails the group’s (16.5%, 13.2% and 14.3%) [3][9][18]. EBITDA by segment is not published for carbon black, power or battery. The rest-of-group figure for FY2026 is ₹920 crore. It matches the company’s EBITDA per tonne of ₹14,939 on 618,956 t (₹925 crore), so that per-tonne figure already includes power and corporate costs [14].

web_blocks.html: Two further limits matter. First, the Integrated Report prints a “segment mix” for FY2026 of 50% tyres, 27% performance chemicals, 13% water, detergent and oil and gas chemicals, and 10% specialty chemicals, on a basis it does not state. It cannot be reconciled with the audited split of 79.5% carbon black and 17.6% chemicals, so we use the audited note for revenue shares [3]. Second, specialty black’s share of profit is not published. The CFO said in July and October 2023 that it earns about 2 to 2.5 times the EBITDA per tonne of tyre grades [25][26]. If performance chemicals earn the tyre-grade rate (our assumption), specialty black at 11.3% of FY2026 volume would carry about ₹187–223 crore, or 20–24%, of carbon black and power EBITDA. That is an illustration from published ratios, not a reported number.

web_blocks.title: Volumes: tyre, performance and specialty blacks

web_blocks.caption: Carbon black sales volume by type, tonnes, consolidated; shares computed
web_blocks.takeaway: Sources: Q4 FY23 call [24], Q4 FY24 update [5], Q4 FY25 update [9], Q4 FY26 update [14] and Q2 FY27 update [18]. Component sums differ from reported totals by 1 t in FY2023 and FY2024 through rounding. Between FY2023 and FY2026 tyre volume grew 13.7% (4.4% a year), performance chemicals 2.1 times and specialty black 1.7 times. The mix shift is therefore mostly into non-tyre industrial rubber black, which gained 10.6 points of volume share. It is not into specialty, which gained 2.2 points. In Q2 FY27 tyre volume fell 17.0%, performance 21.1% and specialty 5.4% [18].

web_blocks.html: Performance chemicals, in PCBL’s vocabulary, are non-tyre rubber blacks: conveyor and transmission belts, hoses, extruded profiles, seals and gaskets, moulded goods, shoe soles, rubber sheets and anti-vibration parts [3]. The industry mix is the inverse of tyres. About 70% of demand is in carcass grades such as N550, N650, N660 and N772, with a typical loading of 23.3 parts of black per 100 parts of rubber [47]. PCBL names no customers here, and the buyers are fragmented. The Managing Director’s remark in our epigraph says why it matters: tyre business is pass-through, while non-tyre prices in India are not, and in recent months have risen [37]. It is also the largest volume cut in H1 FY27 (–15.6%). That suggests it earns less per tonne than tyres or specialty, although the company does not publish the figure.

web_blocks.caption: Aquapharm sales volume by sub-segment, tonnes
web_blocks.takeaway: FY figures are from the Integrated Report [3] and H1 figures from the Q2 FY27 update [18]. By revenue, the FY2025 mix was detergents 36%, oil and gas 31%, water treatment 18% and others 15%, with phosphonates more than half of revenue [9]. Aquapharm earned ₹153 of revenue per kg in FY2026 and ₹175 in H1 FY27, against ₹105 per kg for carbon black (segment revenue divided by volume). Its EBITDA was ₹17,153 a tonne in FY2026 against ₹14,939 for carbon black (our arithmetic) [3][14]. The Aquapharm CEO reported on 2 November 2026 that home care rose 7% year on year in Q2. Water solutions and oil and gas each fell 20%, and application-specific rose 15% [40].

web_blocks.caption: Where the revenue and volume go; revenue by customer location, ₹ crore (excluding other operating revenue)
rows: Export share of carbon black volume
North America 50%, Europe 20%, India 17%, rest of world 13%
web_blocks.takeaway: Revenue by location is from the audited notes [3][2], volumes from the quarterly updates [5][9][14][18] and Aquapharm’s regional split from the Integrated Report [3]. Overseas revenue rose 60.7% from FY2024 to FY2026 against 9.0% in India. That is largely because Aquapharm is about 83% overseas (about ₹1,197 crore of FY2026 revenue), which leaves roughly 36% of carbon black and power revenue sold abroad (our arithmetic). The split does not track volumes (India revenue –14.0% in FY2026 while domestic carbon black volume rose 9.1%; overseas revenue +16.2% while exports fell 3.8%). The company does not reconcile them, so we draw no conclusion beyond the 44.5% share. Specialty black is about 70% sold internationally [39].

web_blocks.takeaway: Plant capacities are from the Integrated Report [3]. The company’s earlier plants page shows Mundra at 204,750 MTPA, which with the two specialty lines accounts for the 245 KTPA now shown [19]. The Tamil Nadu plant is 27% of capacity and Mundra 28%. FY2026 production of 619,458 t was 70.4% of year-end capacity. Q2 FY27 volume annualised is 59.6% of 900 KTPA (our arithmetic) [3][18].

web_blocks.caption: Aquapharm manufacturing sites and capacity, MTPA
rows: Phosphonate plant since 2003; polymer capacity 21,800 TPA after the L-45 expansion [21][3]
Commissioned 1987; polymers moved to Mahad, site repurposed for trial production [21][3]
web_blocks.takeaway: The two capacity figures conflict. On 167,000 MTPA, FY2026 sales of 94,445 t are 57% utilisation; on 256,747 MTPA they are 37% (our arithmetic). The gap of about 90,000 t is unexplained. A likely cause is counting multi-stage or intermediate products, but that is our guess. We use 167,000 MTPA as the headline, which is the figure in the Q2 FY27 investor update, and treat Aquapharm’s utilisation as low on either basis [3][18].

web_blocks.title: Seven worked examples, one per segment

web_blocks.html: Each example follows one customer archetype through the chain: who buys, what problem the product solves, exactly what is bought, how it is made and delivered, and how it is priced. PCBL names almost no customers in its filings. Where a name is not disclosed we say so and describe the archetype rather than invent one.

web_blocks.title: Worked example 1: Tyre carbon black (57% of carbon black volume)
paragraphs: Who buys, and the problem. The buyer is a tyre maker, for example an Indian radial-tyre manufacturer supplying carmakers, the replacement market and export customers. PCBL does not name tyre customers in its filings. An older vendor profile lists CEAT, MRF, Apollo, Birla Tyres, Balkrishna, Goodyear, Sumitomo, Bridgestone and Kumho. The Integrated Report says PCBL won an award for domestic delivery at the CEAT Vendor Meet 2026 [74][3]. Customers above 10% of revenue each paid ₹1,958.55 crore in FY2026 (23.9% of group revenue, 30.1% of carbon black revenue), against ₹2,429.40 crore in FY2025 and ₹2,488.75 crore in FY2024. Only the combined figure is given, so how many such customers there are is not disclosed [3][2]. The problem solved is that rubber alone is soft and wears quickly. Carbon black, about 28% of a typical tyre’s weight, gives the tread strength and abrasion resistance [66].

What is bought, how it is made and delivered. Tread compounds use fine, high-surface-area grades from the N220 to N375 families. Carcass, sidewall and inner-liner compounds use coarser N550, N660 and N772 [66]. PCBL measures tread-reactor capacity on N330 and carcass-line capacity on N660 [47]. It also adds CarboNext (precise morphology and dispersion for specialised rubber uses) and ECOZEN, made from recovered materials [3]. In the plant, carbon-rich feedstock oil and preheated air enter a reactor at 1,400–1,900°C, and the oil cracks in milliseconds. Water quenches the reaction, bag filters separate the black, and a molasses solution binds it into pellets that are dried and stored [47]. Supply is just-in-time from plants near tyre makers and ports. As of the 2021 placement document, the company had warehouses at Chennai, Kolkata, Ponda and Medak and decanting stations in Asia, Europe and the USA [47]. The Managing Director says tyre majors are moving “from just-in-time to a more resilient just-in-case approach” [37].

How it is priced, and our read. Mr Koul said on 30 April 2026: “Some are Q minus 1, some are M minus 1. So, there are different pass-through mechanisms. … There is also a significant piece of volume which is based on spot pricing.” [37]. Close to a third of volume is spot [39]. The share under written multi-year contracts is not disclosed, and the 2021 placement document said customers typically do not sign long-term supply agreements [47]. Our read: formula contracts pass feedstock through with a one-quarter or one-month lag. The margin is therefore made in spot sales, mix, exports and power, not in the contract base. Orion, a global peer, indexes about 65% of its volume to feedstock [60].

web_blocks.title: Worked example 2: Specialty and non-tyre carbon black (11% of volume, about 70% sold abroad)
paragraphs: Who buys, and the problem. The buyers are compounders and formulators who need a property a tyre grade cannot give: jetness and colour in engineering plastics, UV protection, electrical conductivity in cables and electrostatic-discharge plastics, purity for food-contact plastics or potable-water pipe, or dispersion in inks and coatings [3]. Picture a European compounder of food-contact polymer or an automotive-coatings formulator. Names are not disclosed. The CFO said on 29 July 2026 that “around 70% of our volumes are sold in international market” and “Most of our customers are strategic customers” [39].

What is bought and how it is made. The portfolio has 110+ grades across tyre, performance and specialty uses, with 40+ new grades in three years [3]. Specialty families in the Integrated Report include medium and high colour furnace blacks for engineering plastics, powder blacks for inks, coatings, adhesives and sealants, and high-purity conductive blacks for batteries, ESD applications and extra-high-voltage cables. They also include VedaBlack for automotive, OEM and powder coatings [3]. Compliance is part of the product: USFDA 21 CFR 178.3297 and EU Regulation 10/2011 for food contact, IS 4984 for HDPE potable-water pipe, REACH registration, and ZDHC MRSL v3.1 Level 1 for seven Palej grades [3][17]. The process is the same oil-furnace route with a special feedstock. Mr Koul said on 2 November 2026 that “the capacity that we have is around 75” against the 132,000 MTPA nameplate because of “feedstock, which is unique for Specialty Chemicals. So that is the barrier.” [40]. FY2026 volume was 69,635 t, up 12% [14].

How it is priced, and our read. Prices by grade are not disclosed. The CFO said in July 2023 that specialty earned “about 2x” and in October 2023 “2 to 2.5x of our tyre grade margin” [25][26]. Orion’s FY2024 filing shows specialty EBITDA of about $440 a tonne against about $282 for rubber black, 1.56 times (our arithmetic) [60]. PCBL says expanding “long-term supply and offtake arrangements with strategic customers” is a priority [40]. On our illustration above, specialty black carries 20–24% of carbon black and power EBITDA on 11% of volume. It is the best part of the carbon black business, and it is supply-constrained, not demand-constrained.

web_blocks.title: Worked example 3: Aquapharm water solutions and phosphonates (16% of Aquapharm volume)
paragraphs: Who buys, and the problem. The buyers are water-treatment programme providers and plant operators: cooling-tower and boiler treatment at refineries and petrochemical complexes, and desalination plants. PCBL does not name them; Aquapharm’s named customers are the home-care brands in Example 5. The problem is scale and corrosion. Phosphonates bind calcium and iron ions so that insoluble scale cannot form, and they protect iron and steel in cooling circuits. They are used in cooling water, desalination, oil fields and reverse-osmosis plants as anti-scalants [68]. The Aquapharm CEO says demand is strong across regions, with data centres a new use. He adds that the Gulf is shifting from thermal desalination to seawater reverse osmosis, which requires fresh account approvals, and that a new three-year anti-scaling contract has been won [39][40].

What is bought and how it is made. The products are HEDP, ATMP and PBTC phosphonates plus polymers such as the biodegradable PESA polymer [3]. HEDP is made from phosphorous acid or phosphorus trichloride with carboxylic precursors, and ATMP from ammonia, phosphorous acid and formaldehyde [67][68]. Phosphorus is the cost driver: yellow phosphorus, acrylic acid and maleic acid rose 48% after the West Asia conflict began in the March 2026 quarter. Yellow-phosphorus backward integration is a stated goal [3]. Mahad is the main plant (198,239 MTPA, with polymer capacity of 21,800 TPA). Jeddah (10,000 MTPA) is the Saudi plant [3].

How it is priced. Prices follow raw materials with a lag. The Aquapharm CEO said a surcharge in Q1 FY27 “helped us keep our spread constant” and that none is assumed for the rest of the year [39]. A useful price anchor is the DGTR’s final findings of 25 September 2026: Chinese HEDP landed at ₹94 a kg and ATMP at ₹87 a kg. The Authority’s worked case has a ₹20 crore annual refinery cooling-water contract using 108–180 kg of HEDP a day (3–5 ppm), costing ₹37–62 lakh a year, or 1.85–3.08% of the contract [57]. The same findings say the domestic industry (Aquapharm and Excel Industries) suffered “financial losses, cash losses, and negative return on capital employed” on both products. They recommend duties of USD 200 a tonne on HEDP and USD 214 on ATMP for five years [57]. The CEO said on 2 November 2026 that “antidumping in India, that’s provisional right now” and that no impact is in the forecast [40].

web_blocks.title: Worked example 4: Aquapharm oil and gas chemicals (25% of Aquapharm volume)
paragraphs: Who buys, and the problem. The buyers are US oilfield-service companies and operators. They need chemicals for hydraulic fracturing, drilling, stimulation and production: scale control, corrosion control and microbial control [3]. PCBL does not name them, and Aquapharm said in August 2024 that it held less than 1% of global oil and gas chemicals [29]. It now has a presence in Midland and North Dakota, approval to sell in New Mexico, and product approvals in Latin America [36][39].

What is bought and how it is made. The products are imidazoline corrosion inhibitors, quaternary ammonium compounds (quats), triazine and other biocides, and phosphonate scale inhibitors. Aquapharm also took a first commercial order for a synthetic thickener in Q2 FY27 [3][40]. The Texas plant (36,000 MTPA, producing since 2019) makes the established products [3][21]. Qualification is slow: on 2 November 2026 the company was still “advancing customer qualifications for our biocides and corrosion inhibitors with key U.S. oil and gas operators” [40].

How it is priced, and our read. Some customers’ prices are linked to feedstock with a one-quarter or one-month lag [37]. Demand follows rig counts and frac spreads. The Integrated Report blames lower US counts for the FY2026 volume fall of 19.5% (23,640 t against 29,361 t), and H1 FY27 volume fell a further 28.4% [3][18]. Management said on 30 April 2026 that drilling activity “should rise by around 30% at current crude” [36]. On 29 July 2026 the Aquapharm CEO cited “customer inventory overhangs” and said the segment was down 35% year on year in Q1 but up 50% on the prior quarter [39]. Our read: this is Aquapharm’s most cyclical and least-qualified line. We assume little contribution until the qualifications complete.

web_blocks.title: Worked example 5: Home care and green chelates (41% of Aquapharm volume)
paragraphs: Who buys, and the problem. The buyers are global consumer-goods formulators of laundry, dishwash and surface-cleaning products. The Chairman named Procter & Gamble, Unilever, Henkel and Reckitt on 28 November 2023, and ICRA names P&G, Henkel, Ecolab and Unilever [27][42]. Hard-water metals weaken detergents, so formulations carry a chelating agent. Phosphonates do that job and also act as scale inhibitor and bleach stabiliser [68]. Formulators are moving toward biodegradable alternatives, though. The Aquapharm CEO says Europe “is a bit of a headwind as the market gear shifts towards green chelates” [39].

What is bought and how it is made. The products are phosphonates (HEDP, ATMP, PBTC), polymers and green chelates, meaning GLDA, MGDA and IDS, which the Chairman described as “biodegradable chelating agents, which improve detergency” [3][27]. In detergent, the DGTR’s illustration uses about 200 g of HEDP per 100 kg of product, ₹19 of chelant against ₹5,500 of product cost (0.34%) [57]. Our inference is that switching a chelant saves a formulator little, while a failed batch costs a lot, so approvals are sticky. In Q3 FY26 Aquapharm received its first formal GLDA allocation from P&G for MENA and Europe and was on track to supply Henkel in Europe from Q1 FY27. IDS received REACH registration and started commercial supplies in Europe [35].

How it is priced, and our read. Some contracts are linked to raw materials with a lag, and a surcharge was used to hold the spread in Q1 FY27 [37][39]. On 29 July 2026 management said green-chelate order booking was “running ahead of our current capacity” and that a new facility was under discussion [39]. Against that, the Chairman’s November 2023 plan was to lift green chelates 20 times in five years from 3,300 t. An analyst noted in August 2024 that they were only about 1% of sales, and the Integrated Report now targets a rise from under 5% to over 10% of contribution by FY2027 [27][29][3]. Home care volume rose 11.1% in FY2026 but only 1.2% in H1 FY27 [3][18]. We rate this the most promising Aquapharm line, but its scale is still small.

web_blocks.title: Worked example 6: Advanced battery materials (no revenue yet)
paragraphs: Who buys, and the problem. The intended buyers are lithium-ion cell and anode makers. PCBL names none and says it is advancing validation “with leading battery manufacturers” [3]. The problem is energy density: silicon stores about ten times the charge of graphite (3,579 against 372 mAh/g) but expands by up to 300% in use, which cracks electrodes. Silicon must therefore be engineered into a carbon composite [40]. Conductive carbon additives are the other need, to carry current through the electrode.

What is bought and how it is made. Three products are in play. Nano-silicon is made by Nanovace (51% PCBL, with the Australian partner Kinaltek, through Kindia, holding 49%) through a proprietary single-step chemical-reduction process. An 80-tonne pilot at Palej was due live by March 2026, and on 2 November 2026 it had “started creating some samples”, now aimed at silicon-carbon composites. Mr Koul added that “Graphite is not what we are looking at this stage” [3][35][40]. Energia 1040 and 1070 super-conductive blacks come from a 1,000 MTPA line at Palej that is operational, with no customer named [3][39]. Acetylene black (4,000 MTPA at Mundra, technology from Ningxia Jinhua, with approval under the ECMS framework) is in engineering. Management said in April 2025 that global demand is about 70,000 MTPA with 90% of supply from China [3][32][40].

How it is priced, and our read. There is no price yet. Management’s targets are about $20,000 a tonne of realisation and $10,000 of EBITDA a tonne for the super-conductive grade, worth ₹85–100 crore of EBITDA at peak (as reported by SMIFS). For a 2,000-tonne nano-silicon plant at full use, management points to roughly ₹1,700 crore of revenue with “almost 50%” to profit, reached only at the end of FY2029 or early FY2030 [65][35]. That implies about ₹8.5 crore of revenue per tonne of nano-silicon (our arithmetic), which no customer has validated. The segment lost ₹0.15 crore in FY2026, and PCBL has put ₹228 crore into Nanovace convertibles. Group14 and Sila, funded leaders, are only now opening or about to open factories [3][69][80]. This is an option, not an earner.

web_blocks.title: Worked example 7: Captive power (2.9% of revenue, 24% of segment profit)
paragraphs: Who buys, and the problem. The buyers are the grid, power exchanges and, under bilateral contracts, group and third-party utilities. Related parties took ₹120.08 crore of power in FY2026, which is 70.6% of the parent’s power sales of ₹170.13 crore and 55.6% of group power sales of ₹216.16 crore. The counterparties are not named in the note, and the rates are stated to be at arm’s length [3]. The problem solved is waste. The off-gas from the reactor, with a calorific value of about 650–700 kcal per cubic metre, has no other use, so each plant burns it to raise steam and power [47].

What is made and how it is delivered. The five plants hold 122 MW of co-generation (30 MW Durgapur, 32 Mundra, 24 Chennai, 19 Palej, 17 Kochi), with 12 MW more in Tamil Nadu due in FY2027 [18]. FY2026 generation was a record 839 MU (+13.4%), of which 511 MU, or 61%, was sold. Q2 FY27 was 186 MU generated and 108 MU sold [3][18]. The CFO said on 2 November 2026: “PCBL about 40% of the power that we generate, we use captively and 60% is available for sale” and “the generation of power actually is dependent on the carbon black production level” [40].

How it is priced, and our read. Price is the grid tariff, not cost: ₹4.24 per unit in FY2026 (+9.84%) and ₹5.34 in Q2 FY27 against ₹3.76 a year earlier. Bilateral contracts were 43% of merchant sales against 31% a year before [3][18]. On 5.6% of segment assets the segment earned a 40.8% pre-tax return. Our read: power is a high-return by-product whose profit depends on tariffs PCBL does not control and on carbon black output. The related-party share is a governance point for Chapter 6, not a reason to discount the cash.

web_blocks.title: Which segments carry the economics, and which are options

web_blocks.takeaway: Segment shares are from the audited note [3]; the classification is ours.

web_blocks.html: Today the economics sit in carbon black and power. Tyre and performance blacks are the volume base and earn a spread that moves with crude and freight (Chapter 3). Specialty black is the highest-quality slice and the one that can lift the per-tonne figure, and power adds a quarter of segment profit on a small asset base. Aquapharm is a real business, with ₹1,443 crore of revenue, 265+ customers and a top-three phosphonate position. On today’s numbers, though, it returns less than the cost of the debt used to buy it. We see a turnaround with identifiable catalysts (a provisional anti-dumping duty, green-chelate approvals at P&G and Henkel, a new chief executive, lower raw-material prices). We put only about a one-in-four chance on Aquapharm reaching ₹250 crore of annual EBITDA within two years, because its water and oil and gas volumes are falling and its capacity is half-used. Battery materials are an option. For silicon, which needs customer qualification and then a commercial plant, we would give no better than roughly one chance in five of qualified commercial supply by FY2029. Conductive carbons have better odds because they extend a skill PCBL already has, but they are small, at 1,000 to 4,000 tonnes.

What would change our mind is any one of three things. The first is disclosed specialty-black margins that confirm a 2–2.5 times premium at 80,000 t or more of volume. The second is Aquapharm segment profit before interest and tax above ₹100 crore a year (about 2.4% of segment assets, still below the cost of debt but a visible turn). The third is a named battery customer completing qualification. A fall of specialty volume below 60,000 t, or a further fall in Aquapharm’s volume, would move us the other way.

book_paragraphs: Imagine standing at the Mundra plant gate, watching a tanker discharge feedstock oil. Everything this company sells starts with a version of that oil, and the difference between the segments is what happens next. Let us follow the largest stream first: tyre carbon black, about 57 percent of what PCBL sold in FY2026. The oil is atomised into a reactor at 1,400 to 1,900 degrees, cracks in a few milliseconds, is quenched with water, filtered out of the gas, and glued into small pellets with molasses. Then it is loaded onto a truck or a railcar for a tyre maker, who needs it at the factory just in time. Carbon black is about 28 percent of a tyre’s weight, and fine grades such as N330 make the tread resist wear, while coarser N660 builds the carcass. Who exactly buys? Our filings do not say. An older vendor profile names CEAT, MRF, Apollo and others, and the company reports an award at the CEAT Vendor Meet 2026, but the only firm number is that customers above ten percent of revenue paid ₹1,958 crore in FY2026, nearly a quarter of group revenue.

How is that carbon black priced? Here I want you to hear it from the Managing Director, Nilesh Koul, on 30 April 2026: “Some are Q minus 1, some are M minus 1. So, there are different pass-through mechanisms.” In plain words, the contract price follows the feedstock cost with a lag of a quarter or a month. “There is also a significant piece of volume,” he added, “which is based on spot pricing.” Management says close to a third of volume is spot. What does that mean for you as an owner? That the contract base gives PCBL a spread per tonne, but the swings, and the profit above that spread, come from the spot third, from exports, from specialty and from power. And the share under multi-year written contracts? Not disclosed, which is itself information.

Before we go further, step back and see where the profit lives, because the brochure and the audited note tell different stories. The audited segment note says carbon black was 79.5 percent of FY2026 revenue and 73.8 percent of segment profit, but its profit before interest and tax fell from ₹1,042 crore to ₹721 crore in a single year while its revenue fell only 4 percent. Power was 2.9 percent of revenue and 24.4 percent of segment profit. Aquapharm, the chemicals segment, was 17.6 percent of revenue and 1.8 percent of profit. The Integrated Report also prints a pie chart of 50 percent tyres, 27 percent performance, 13 percent water and oil chemicals and 10 percent specialty, on a basis it does not explain, and it cannot be reconciled with the audited note. When two documents from the same company disagree, which do you trust? The one that auditors signed. And for EBITDA by segment? Not published, except for Aquapharm: 14.0 percent of group EBITDA in FY2025, 15.0 percent in FY2026 and 12.5 percent in the first half of FY27, always less than its share of revenue because its margin is lower.

Keep one habit as you read the next few paragraphs. For each product, ask four plain questions: who buys it, what problem does it solve for them, what exactly do they order, and who sets the price? A company that can answer all four in writing usually has a business; a company that can only answer the first with a logo slide usually has a story. PCBL answers the second and third very well, the fourth partly, and the first rarely, because it names almost no customers. That is not unusual for an industrial supplier, but it limits what you and I can verify, and I will say so each time.

Performance chemicals are the next stream, and they surprised me. This is non-tyre rubber black: the filler in conveyor belts, hoses, seals, shoe soles and anti-vibration mounts. Its share of PCBL’s volume went from 21 percent in FY2023 to 31 percent in FY2026, doubling in tonnes, while tyres grew only 4 percent a year. So the story that PCBL is moving up to specialty is only partly true; the bigger move was into industrial rubber blacks, which are sold more on the spot market and which the company does not give a margin for. When the first half of FY27 forced a choice, this was the volume it cut most, down 15.6 percent. Mr Koul’s remark in the epigraph explains why: in tyres the price is a pass-through, but in non-tyre markets it is not, and in recent months it has risen.

Specialty black is the part I would want to own. Think of a European compounder making food-contact plastic, or a coatings maker needing a jet-black pigment for car paint. For them the product is a grade with a certificate, such as US FDA 21 CFR 178.3297 or the EU food-contact regulation, and a customer must qualify it before it buys. The CFO, Raj Gupta, told investors in October 2023 that PCBL makes “2 to 2.5x of our tyre grade margin” on specialty, and Orion’s own filing shows about $440 a tonne against $282 for rubber black. If performance chemicals earn the tyre rate, my arithmetic says specialty is about 11 percent of volume and 20 to 24 percent of carbon black and power EBITDA. But look at the constraint, in Mr Koul’s words on 2 November 2026: “the capacity that we have is around 75 … feedstock, which is unique for Specialty Chemicals. So that is the barrier.” The nameplate says 132,000 tonnes; the working number is about 75,000. Supply, not demand, is the limit.

Power is the quiet one. Every reactor produces a hot gas that can burn, and PCBL burns it to make steam and electricity: 122 megawatts across five plants, 839 million units in FY2026, of which 511 million were sold. The CFO put it simply on 2 November 2026: about 40 percent is used captively and 60 percent is available for sale, so “higher realization actually pushes up the bottom line for us.” The result is striking: power was 2.9 percent of revenue and 24.4 percent of segment profit in FY2026, a 41 percent pre-tax return on its assets. Two cautions. Its profit tracks carbon black output, which fell in the second quarter, and about 71 percent of the parent’s power sales went to related parties, which I will examine in Chapter 6.

Now ask where these products go, and where they are made. About 44.5 percent of FY2026 revenue came from customers outside India, and Aquapharm alone is about 83 percent overseas, with North America half of its revenue. Carbon black exports were 38 percent of volume in FY2026 and were deliberately cut to 31 percent in the second quarter of FY27, because the CFO preferred to let low-margin Southeast Asian orders go. The five carbon black plants are Durgapur, the oldest, at 163,000 tonnes; Kochi at 93,000; Palej at 142,000, which also houses the research centre and the new super-conductive line; Mundra at 245,000, beside the port; and Chennai at 237,000, which alone is 27 percent of the capacity. Together they total 880,000 tonnes, or 900,000 after the Mundra specialty line, against FY2026 production of 619,458 tonnes, which is about 70 percent of the year-end figure. For Aquapharm, one page of the same annual report says 167,000 tonnes and another says 256,747, so utilisation is either 57 percent or 37 percent. I cannot reconcile the two, and I will not pretend to.

Now cross the road to Aquapharm, and let me start with a ₹20 crore refinery cooling-water contract, because India’s trade-remedy authority wrote it down. A cooling circuit scales up and corrodes unless it is dosed. At 3 to 5 parts per million, the operator adds 108 to 180 kilograms of HEDP a day, which at the ₹94 a kilogram Chinese landed price costs ₹37 to 62 lakh a year, under 3.1 percent of the contract. That is Aquapharm’s core water-solutions business: phosphonates that bind calcium and iron so scale cannot form. Is it a good business? The Authority’s own findings say Indian producers made cash losses on HEDP and ATMP in the period because Chinese imports landed below their cost of sales; it recommended duties of $200 and $214 a tonne in September 2026. The Aquapharm CEO, Rohit Narang, told analysts on 2 November that “antidumping in India, that’s provisional right now” and that he has built none of it into the forecast.

Water solutions volume fell 12 percent in FY2026, and oil and gas fell 19.5 percent. The oil and gas story is the one I would watch most closely for disappointment. Its customers are American oilfield service companies who need corrosion inhibitors, biocides and scale inhibitors for fracturing and drilling, and qualification with them takes time. Management said in April 2026 that drilling should rise about 30 percent at current crude; by July Mr Narang was describing “customer inventory overhangs”, and first-half FY27 volume was down 28 percent. Aquapharm said in August 2024 that it had less than one percent of this global market. That is a growth option, and also the reason a 25 percent slice of Aquapharm’s volume is the least certain 25 percent.

The most appealing line is home care and its green chelates. A laundry-detergent maker, whether Procter & Gamble, Henkel or Unilever, needs a chelating agent to tame hard water, and phosphonates have done it for decades. But Europe is shifting to biodegradable alternatives, GLDA and MGDA, and the Chairman said on 28 November 2023 that the plan was to lift green chelates twenty-fold from 3,300 tonnes in five years. By February 2026 Aquapharm announced its first formal GLDA allocation from P&G, and by July the company said order booking was “running ahead of our current capacity.” That is progress, and it is also a long way from twenty times. In detergent the chelant is a fraction of one percent of product cost, so once approved a supplier is sticky, but approval is what takes years.

Last, batteries, and I want you to feel the physics. Silicon holds about ten times the charge of graphite, but it swells up to 300 percent when it charges, so a battery maker cannot simply use it. PCBL’s answer is Nanovace, a 51 percent joint venture, making nano-silicon in a pilot at Palej, now moving to silicon-carbon composites, plus super-conductive carbon blacks and, later, acetylene black from Mundra. Management’s targets are eye-catching: about $20,000 a tonne of realisation for the super-conductive grade and roughly ₹1,700 crore of revenue from a 2,000-tonne nano-silicon plant at full use, which works out at ₹8.5 crore a tonne. No customer has validated any of it. The segment lost ₹0.15 crore in FY2026 and holds ₹246 crore of assets. Call it an option, and an expensive one in time.

So where does the money actually come from? My honest ranking has four tiers. First, tyre and performance blacks supply the volume and a thin spread. Second, specialty black and power supply the quality: perhaps a fifth to a quarter of EBITDA from specialty, and a quarter of segment profit from power. Third, Aquapharm supplies ₹1,443 crore of revenue but only a 0.4 percent pre-tax return on ₹4,226 crore of segment assets in FY2026. Fourth, batteries supply hope. I put about one chance in four on Aquapharm reaching ₹250 crore of EBITDA within two years, and no better than one in five on silicon reaching commercial supply by FY2029. Those are judgments, not facts, and the evidence that would change them is listed in the trigger above.

Notice what ties these seven examples together: in every one, price is set by something outside PCBL’s hands, whether feedstock, grid tariffs, Chinese landed prices or a rig count, and what PCBL controls is the grade, the qualification and the plant. In Chapter 3 we turn to how those products reach customers, how the pass-through formula and the working-capital cycle work, and what a ₹100 of revenue becomes by the time it reaches free cash flow.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: I find the DGTR’s cooling-water arithmetic the most useful number in this chapter. A ₹20 crore contract spends perhaps ₹37 to 62 lakh on the chemical that keeps the circuit from scaling. The chemical is cheap relative to what it protects, so buyers care more about reliable supply and proven quality than about a saving of a few rupees a kilogram. That is exactly why switching is slow in specialty chemicals and also why Chinese landed prices below cost can still hurt: the buyer will switch for a lower price only until the first quality failure.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Look at who gets the label ‘specialty’. PCBL’s specialty black is 11 percent of volume and perhaps a fifth of carbon black EBITDA, a real premium. Aquapharm’s ‘specialty chemicals’ are 17.6 percent of revenue and 1.8 percent of segment profit. The word on the brochure tells you nothing about the return; only the segment note does.

book_callouts.title: Engine, quality, turnaround, option
book_callouts.text: Sort every segment of a diversified industrial into four boxes: the engine that supplies volume and thin spreads, the quality contributor that lifts per-tonne returns, the turnaround that has capital invested but a return below its cost, and the option that costs time and has no revenue. Then ask of each box what evidence would move it up or down. For PCBL the answers are specialty margins disclosed, Aquapharm segment profit above ₹100 crore, and a named battery customer.
